final_recommendation: The room chose protracted multi-jurisdictional litigation over settlement. Bondholder counsel rejected FINMA's written grandfathering offer and committed to discovery targeting board memos, betting that SEC/EU investigations will force retroactive contract rewriting. Institutional investors warned they would liquidate AT1 holdings regardless, and insurance observers confirmed a 36+ month claims tail with systemic repricing already locked in.
minority_objections: FINMA legal repeatedly offered forward-only contract language plus written grandfathering as a 90-day settlement path
Insurance observer warned that formal investigations extend rather than compress the tail, making discovery economically irrational
Institutional investor stated they would sell AT1 holdings this week regardless of discovery outcomes because forward-only language doesn't fix existing holdings
key_conflicts: Bondholder counsel demanded retroactive contract rewriting; FINMA and insurers said this breaks capital structure assumptions and is unpriceable
Counsel believed board memos would expose legal fragility; FINMA argued memos validate their emergency-powers defense
Institutional investors needed immediate market stabilization; counsel prioritized long-term precedent reset over short-term portfolio protection
key_concessions: FINMA offered written grandfathering isolating Credit Suisse write-down to insolvency-plus-government-support facts
FINMA committed to prospective guidance narrowing viability-event triggers for future AT1 issuances
Bondholder counsel acknowledged forward-only language was on the table but rejected it as insufficient
red_lines: Bondholder counsel: will not settle without retroactive term rewriting or global AT1 contract language reset
Insurance observer: carriers will not price a tail predicated on retroactive capital structure amendments
Institutional investor: will liquidate AT1 holdings if settlement doesn't address existing bond repricing within days
FINMA: will not issue statement contradicting the contractual basis (paragraph 5.1) they are defending in court
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: The room never resolved whether SEC/EU investigations would actually mandate contract changes or merely extend defense costs
No participant modeled the scenario where discovery validates FINMA's legal process, eliminating bondholder leverage entirely
The political feasibility of retroactive contract rewriting across the entire European AT1 market was asserted but never tested
Bondholder counsel's own litigation defense costs hitting reinsurance caps within 24 months was raised but not integrated into the decision calculus
downstream_risk_variables: AT1 market repricing velocity: institutional investors stated they would liquidate within the week, creating immediate contagion
Reinsurance accumulation: 36+ month tail across SEC/EU/Swiss proceedings with D&O and E&O claims accumulating in parallel
Regulatory precedent: whether Basel/SEC/EU use this case to mandate tighter AT1 trigger language globally or treat it as Swiss-specific
Discovery outcomes: whether FINMA board memos expose legal fragility or validate emergency-powers defense
Settlement window closure: FINMA's written offer expires if not accepted; no clarity on whether it can be reopened post-discovery
uncertainty_notes: The room terminated without resolving the core strategic question: whether discovery would produce a regulatory mandate forcing global AT1 contract changes, or merely extend a multi-year tail while institutional investors liquidate and the market reprices contagion. Bondholder counsel bet on the former; every other participant warned of the latter. No mechanism was established to test this assumption before committing to the discovery path.

marker_evidence.litigation_likelihood: Litigation was the dominant path chosen: bondholder counsel mobilized full resources, filed emergency interdict, initiated discovery targeting FINMA board memos, and rejected settlement offers explicitly to pursue multi-year court proceedings
marker_evidence.regulatory_legitimacy_challenge: The room built a sustained challenge to FINMA's legal basis: attacking the emergency ordinance as procedurally defective, questioning whether paragraph 5.1 was ex-post-facto lawmaking, and coordinating SEC/EU regulatory scrutiny of board decision-making
marker_evidence.creditor_hierarchy_controversy: The equity-preserved-while-AT1-wiped inversion drove every major exchange: institutional investors threatened portfolio liquidation over it, counsel made it the core of their legal challenge, and FINMA's inability to narrow the precedent was the deal-breaker
marker_evidence.market_confidence_damage: AT1 market repricing was a central, decision-driving force: institutional investors stated they would liquidate holdings within the week, credit analysts warned of 300-bps repricing contagion, and insurance observers confirmed systemic write-down risk was already being priced across all European bank AT1
marker_evidence.claims_tail: The multi-year claims tail was developed in granular detail: insurance observer specified 36+ months of defense costs across SEC/EU/Swiss proceedings, modeled D&O and E&O accumulation, and stated the tail was already locked in and unpriceable under counsel's retroactive-rewriting strategy
marker_evidence.financial_lines_relevance: D&O and E&O exposure was a concrete, recurring theme: insurance observer warned of reinsurance accumulation across three jurisdictions, stated carriers were already modeling the tail and would not price retroactive capital structure amendments, and flagged director liability claims as a specific downstream risk
